**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The rule is satisfied by absence, which is the preferred position — not merely the fallback.

What I checked:
- **Targeted searches** for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee", "forfeit", "minimum annual", "as compensation for" — all returned no hits (the only "minimum" hits are insurance limits in §11.6).
- **Full read of Article 12** (Term and Termination) to catch an unlabelled exit payment. §12.3 gives AbbVie termination for convenience on 90 days' notice with **no** termination fee. The consequences provisions (§§12.6–12.8, 12.10) are confined to licence reversion, product wind-down and payment of amounts already accrued for pre-termination milestones/Net Sales — ordinary accrued consideration, not a pre-agreed liquidated sum.
- **All "AbbVie shall pay" hits** — upfront, milestones and royalties under §§6.1–6.5, i.e. ordinary purchase consideration, plus §7 patent-extension expenses. None is a sanction.

Two points noted in the rationale rather than flagged:
- **§6.10 default interest** (the planner's item to confirm) is expressly **mutual** — "If any payment due to either Party ... such paying Party shall pay interest thereon" — and interest of this kind is a time-value remedy, not liquidated damages. The rate is redacted (`[***]`), so I could not verify it is commercially standard; I flagged that limitation rather than asserting compliance on the number, but the mutuality means it cannot operate as a one-way penalty on us.
- **§12.9** preserves ordinary law/equity remedies mutually instead of fixing a pre-agreed amount.

Worth noting for the wider review: this is a pharma development-and-option agreement rather than a services deal, so the customer-side risk here sits in reversion obligations (§12.7, where AbbVie grants back reversion IP and performs transfer obligations, several terms redacted) rather than in liquidated damages. Those non-monetary exit burdens fall outside this rule but may deserve attention under a reversion or termination-assistance rule if the playbook has one.
